title_original: Lotus L. Kang wins 2026 Sobey Art Award
excerpt_original: The artist will receive CAD $100,000 for the grand prize

blocks.alt: Lotus L Kang. Photo: Carolyne Loreé Teston
blocks.caption: Photo: Carolyne Loreé Teston

blocks.text: Lotus L. Kang has won the grand prize for the 2026 Sobey Art Award, the National Gallery of Canada (NGC) and the Sobey Art Foundation (SAF) have announced. She will receive CAD $100,000 for the top prize.

Born in Toronto, Canada, Kang’s work unfolds across sculpture, photography and site-responsive installation. Through her approach to materiality, her work considers impermanence, inheritance, memory, and time. ‘The recognition of this prize means that askew ideas are worth pursuing. Art is essential to life, progress and love’, Kang said in response to receiving the award.

‘In selecting Lotus L. Kang, the Jury recognizes the commitment and rigour demonstrated in her practice for well over a decade. Through installations using unfixed photographic film, cast and found objects, and fabricated armatures, her practice resists the stabilizing impulses traditionally associated with photography’, said Jonathan Shaughnessy, Director of Curatorial Initiatives at the NGC and Chair of the 2026 Sobey Art Award Jury.

Kang is the 23rd winner of the Sobey Art Award, which looks to celebrate artists who are at a critical juncture in their careers. Previous grand prize winners include Abbas Akhavan (2015), Jeremy Shaw (2016) and Stephanie Comilang (2019).
